title: Cap. IX Arg. 12 Sol: who prays for one God precisely wills not to save? — secret of election/reprobation unknown; absolute reprobation is not 'damn Judas whether he believe or not'
pass_a_gloss: But they still urge; Who can bring it into his mind that he should pray for the salvation of him whom God precisely wills not to be saved, when the Apostle with this argument sharpens us unto praying for all, because God wills all to be saved? I answer first, God is not wont to lay open unto men this secret of election and reprobation; our actions therefore neither ought nor can be conformed unto an unknown rule. Secondly, in the decree of absolute or precise reprobation, as they speak, God has not thus established with himself, I will damn Judas, whether he believe not or believe, but, I will not so have mercy on Judas that he be softened, that he believe, that finally in fact he be converted and saved — as in the decree of absolute predestination God does not say, I will save Peter, whether he believe or not, but I will so have mercy on Peter that he believe, that he repent, that he be saved. If therefore by precise and absolute predestination and reprobation they think we understand I-know-not-what cutting-off of means from the end, they fight their own chimera, not our sentence.
pass_b_english: But they still urge: Who can bring himself to pray for the salvation of one whom God precisely wills not to save, when the Apostle sharpens us to pray for all because God wills all to be saved? I answer first: God does not usually lay open to men this secret of election and reprobation; so our actions neither ought nor can be conformed to an unknown rule. Second: in the decree of absolute or precise reprobation, as they speak, God has not settled with himself, I will damn Judas whether he believe or not — but, I will not so have mercy on Judas that he be softened, believe, and in fact be converted and saved. Just so in absolute predestination God does not say, I will save Peter whether he believe or not — but, I will so have mercy on Peter that he believe, repent, and be saved. If by precise absolute predestination and reprobation they think we mean some cutting of means from the end, they fight their own chimera, not our view.
source_text: Sed adhuc urgent; Quis potest in animum inducere ut pro ejus salute oret, quem Deus praecise nolit servari, cum Apostolus hoc argumento nos acuat ad precandum pro omnibus, quia Deus vult omnes salvos fieri? Respondeo primo, Deus non solet hoc arcanum electionis et reprobationis hominibus patefacere; actiones igitur nostrae ad regulam incognitam nec debent, nec possunt conformari. Secundo, in decreto reprobationis absolutae sive praecisae, ut illi loquuntur, Deus non sic statuit apud se, Ego damnabo Judam, sive non credat sive credat, sed, Ego non ita miserebor Judae, ut emolliatur, ut credat, ut denique de facto convertatur et servetur — sicuti in decreto praedestinationis absolutae Deus non dicit, Ego salvabo Petrum, sive credat sive non, sed Ego ita miserebor Petri, ut credat, ut poeniteat, ut servetur. Si igitur per praecisam et absolutam praedestinationem et reprobationem putant nos intelligere nescio quam praecisionem mediorum a fine, chimaeram suam, non sententiam nostram oppugnant.
